div.p: This paper generalizes the load scaling techniques proposed in 4, 5 for xed-priority real-time applications. A framework is proposed to adjust the system workload by relating the criticality and exibility of a process to the resource allocation problem. A l o ad adjustment procedure based on the approximation algorithm 10 is proposed to maximize the system pro t in an on-line fashion. When the list of allowable con gurations is implicitly given by scalable periodic processes, the corresponding load ltering problems is shown to be NP-complete. We also prove the upper bound of the system pro t and provide a mechanism to balance the schedulability and the maximum pro t of the system.

div.head: Introduction
div.p: Most existing work on real-time resource allocation assumes that real-time processes have xed timing parameters such as periods, deadlines, and minimum separation 7, 8, 9 , 1 3 , 1 4 . The resource scheduling problem is to determine whether a scheduler exists the feasibility problem or whether a given scheduling policy can meet the timing requirements of the set of processes the schedulability problem. Although much progress has been made in regard to both problems, there are relatively few results in the case where the processes may c hange their timing parameters in reaction to the environment.

Kuo and Mok 4, 5 proposed a framework for discussing how to adjust the workloads so as to handle Supported in part by research grants from the National Science Council under Grant NSC84-2213-E-194-037 and Ministry of Economic A airs under Grant 88-EC-2A-17-0209 periodic processes whose timing parameters vary with time. In particular, they showed that the real-time resource allocation problem can be reformulated to model the adaptive nature of the processes to handle dynamic objects, overload recovery, and fault tolerance. Wang and Lin 15 proposed a formal model of the adaptive processes and derived the basic theory and scheduling algorithms for them. Their study was motivated by the resource allocation problems for a radar system with adaptive sensors 1 . Sides 12 considered a realtime data acquisition and display system in response to the requirements of the system-wide adaptability t o changes in the data stream. This paper generalizes the load scaling techniques proposed in 4, 5 by relating both the criticality and exibility of a process to the resource allocation problem. We propose a load adjustment procedure based on the approximation algorithm 10 to maximize the system pro t in an on-line fashion. When the list of allowable con gurations is implicitly given by scalable periodic processes, the corresponding load ltering problems is shown to be NP-complete. We also prove the upper bound of the system pro t and provide a mechanism to balance the schedulability and the maximum pro t of the system.

The rest of the paper is organized as follows. Section 2 shows the NP-Completeness of the period assignment problem and describes an e cient approximation algorithm for the problem. We then propose load adjustment procedures which maximize the system pro t in an on-line fashion. Section 3 presents an upper bound of the system pro t that any load scaling techniques may a c hieve. We also propose guidelines to adjust the system workload and, at the same time, to maximize the system pro t. Section 4 is the conclusion.
2 Weighted Period Assignment Problem

div.head: Problem statement
div.p: In 4, 5 , Kuo and Mok proposed a load scaling technique to systematically and gracefully degrade the workload of a system by adjusting the timing parameters of processes. In particular, the technique minimizes the number of fundamental frequencies from which processes are assigned periods. They also showed that a process set with periods selected from a less number of fundamental frequencies is more likely to be scheduled in a xed-priority system because of the higher achievable utilization factor of the process set. Although the load scaling technique proposed in 4, 5 can be used to recon gure a system workload at run time or in the design phase of the system, the processes are assumed to be equally important. However, if the workload is so heavy such that there is no way t o make the entire process set schedulable, a natural solution is to select a subset of processes which are more likely to be schedulable and the pro t of the system is maximized. These observations underline the goals of this research.

Since the weighted period assignment problem is NP-Complete, no polynomial time algorithm is likely to exist for nding the best period assignment. An ecient approximation algorithms with good performance bounds was reported in 10 :

The weighted period assignment problem has two quantities to be optimized: the harmonic base set and the sum of process weights. We choose to maximize the sum of process weights and keep a xed bound K of the harmonic base because the sum of process weights represents the best interests or the maximum pro t of the system. In other words, the approximation algorithms should pick up a collection T 0 of processes from a given scalable process set such that there is an allowable con guration for T 0 that has a harmonic base size no larger than K, and the total process weight i n T 0 is maximized.

The main approximation algorithm is called Period-Assignment and works in two stages. In the rst stage, the procedure Reduction reduces an instance of the weighted period assignment problem to an instance of a v ariation of the set covering problem, where every set is assigned a weight. In the second stage, the procedure Approximate greedily selects harmonic chains with the largest process weight and assigns processes proper periods and computation times. Note that the weight o f a set harmonic chain is not xed during the execution of the approximation algorithm.

div.head: On-Line Adjustment Procedure
div.p: With the e cient approximation algorithm reported in 10 , a technical question here is when and how to apply the weighted load scaling techniques in an on-line fashion. The purpose of this section is to propose an on-line load adjustment procedure based on the approximation algorithm and evaluate its performance.

We s a y that the system experiences a mode change at time t if some process asks to change its workload, i.e. timing constraints, at time t. Even if load scaling can be done instantly at time t, the system must decide when to apply the new period and computation time assignments determined by the approximation algorithms to processes. Let a mode change occur at time t. Three adjustment procedures of periods and computation times are considered in this paper2 :
1. Next-Cycle Adjustment NA: E v ery process uses its new period and computation time at the end of its current period.

2. Temporary Postponement TP: Every process uses its new period and computation time at time t 0 , where t 0 is some time betwen time t and the end of the current period. In this paper, we assume that t 0 is in the middle of time t and the end of the current period. If process has not nished its execution at time t, its remaining computation time is halved, and the deadline of the remaining computation is t 0 .

3. Immediate Adjustment IA: E v ery process uses its new period and computation time at time t. If process has not nished its execution at time t, then is terminated and restarted with the new period and computation time immediately. The rationale behind the IA procedure is to emulate a system which is required to go through adrupt mode changes whenever they are needed. The TP procedure is a compromise of the NA and IA procedures.

div.p: The experiments described in this section are meant to assess the capabilities of the weighted load adjustment techniques in reducing the number of deadline violations for critical processes during run-time. Each process set, which consisted of processes randomly selected from the above four types, was simulated from time 0 to time 3; 000; 000ms. Processes in each process set experienced a mode change every 6 seconds on average. The inter-arrival time was generated by an exponential distribution function. When a mode change happened at time t, the total utilization factor of the process set uctuated no more than 20 of the total utilization factor. No matter how the workload of a process set uctuated, the average utilization factor of each process set was equal to the total utilization factor of the process set at time 0. 3 Weighted Load Filtering: Schedulability versus System Pro t

div.head: De nitions and NP-Completeness
div.p: An alternative way of workload management is to reject less critical processes if the system is overloaded. A mechanism is needed to select a collection of schedulable processes so that the system pro t is maximized.
A CPU utilization bound U can be used to restrict the total workload of the set of selected processes and to guarantee their schedulability. The problem can be formally de ned as follows:

De nition: Weighted Load Filtering Problem Given n weighted scalable periodic processes, T = f 1 ; ; n g and three positive i n tegers K, W, and U, is there an allowable con guration for a subset T 0 T such that the harmonic base of T 0 is no larger than K, the CPU utilization of T 0 is no larger than U, and the sum of process weights in T 0 is no less than W.

Note that a process set with a smaller harmonic base is more likely to be scheduled by the system. The denition of the weighted load ltering problem also gives users exibility in allocating a portion U of the entire CPU time for selecting processes.

div.head: The Upper Bound of System Pro t

An approximation algorithm should pick up a collection T 0 of processes from a given scalable process set such that there is an allowable con guration for T 0 whose harmonic base is no larger than K, the CPU utilization is no larger than U, and the total process weight i n T 0 is maximized.

The technical question then is to nd a collection of processes with a total weight as close to the bound as possible. The astute reader may notice that the sum of the weights of processes in the process set U = f 1 ; ; N u m U g may approximate the bound well. Let MinK be the smallest number of harmonic chains that contains all processes in process set U.

A system with a harmonic base bound K no less than MinK is likely to have a con guration i.e., an assignment of an admissible period to each process to maximize the system pro t weight. However, it was shown in 4, 5 that the problem of determining the best conguration of the processes in U and the minimum value of MinK is NP-Complete in the strong sense. But, with approximate solutions of MinK 4, 5 and system con guration, application engineers are provided valuable information to adjust the timing constraints and or the workload of the system to maximize the system pro t weight.

div.head: Schedulability Bound versus System Pro t
div.p: In the de nition of the weighted load ltering problem, the CPU utilization bound U is de ned independently from the the harmonic base bound K. However, it is a commonly observed phenomenon in real-time scheduling theory that a set of periodic processes is more likely to be schedulable if their periods are harmonically related. This seems to hold regardless of the scheduling policy used. It is also shown in 4, 5 that the least upper bound of the utilization factor for any process set scheduled by a xed priority preemptive scheduling algorithm is K2 1 K , 1. The smaller the size K of the harmonic base, the larger the least upper bound of the utilization factor. These observations suggest iterative adjustments of the harmonic base bound K and the utilization factor bound U if U is a function of K. Suppose that U is a function f of K, i.e., U = fK. The adjustment proceduce of U and K can be as follows:
1. Obtain U which is equal to fK.
2. Let MinK be the minimum number of harmonic chains that contains all processes in process set U.
3. If MinK K Then Stop; otherwise, Let K be MinK, and goto Step 1.

div.head: Conclusion
div.p: This paper generalizes the load scaling techniques proposed in 4, 5 by relating both the criticality and exibility of a process to the resource allocation problem. We propose a load adjustment procedure based on the approximation algorithm 10 to maximize the system pro t in an on-line fashion. When the list of allowable con gurations is implicitly given by scalable periodic processes, the corresponding load ltering problems is shown to be NP-complete. We also prove the upper bound of the system pro t and provide a mechanism to balance the schedulability and the maximum pro t of the system.

The load adjustment approach can be formulated in a variety o f w ays to suit di erent assumptions about how the system should adapt to changes. Although the load adjustment problem is investigated in the context of xed-priority s c heduling, the important idea, however, is that we n o w h a ve a w ay to relate the criticality and exibility of a process to the resource allocation problem. For future research, we will exploit the idea of the sporadic server 13 with the concept of load adjustment techniques. We will also investigate quantitatively how the load adjustment can help improve the schedulability and utilization of a computer system, especially when imprecise data such as audio and video streams are considered.
